newsitem.title: USA: Gore praises U.S. airlines for new safety attitude.
newsitem.headline: Gore praises U.S. airlines for new safety attitude.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore Wednesday praised U.S. airlines for cooperating on safety and security issues as he met families of air crash victims.

Gore held a private meeting with relatives of victims of eight plane crashes dating back to 1983, including TWA Flight 800 that exploded mysteriously off Long Island in July with the deaths of all 230 people aboard.

The meeting was intended to hear concerns and suggestions about improving aviation safety and security ahead of an afternoon meeting of the White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security. Gore chairs the commission but was unable to be at the afternoon meeting because he was attending the funeral in Chicago of Cardinal Joseph Bernardin.
Many relatives have complained of airline delays in getting information about loved ones who died in crashes.

Gore, speaking to reporters after his morning meeting, said he could not discuss past foot-dragging by the industry but added: "I will say that it's a new day and we're finding that the industry is ready to respond, and that's good because they're going to have to respond."

He said of particular note was an industry decision to ask passengers boarding international flights for the name and address of next of kin. Relatives of victims had pressed for the change, which the industry had made reluctantly.

"To their credit as they begin to fully understand how strongly the American people feel and understand that all of them were going to have to do it at the same time, and there was no competitive issue, then they did enter into this agreement," Gore said. "And we're seeing the same kind of new attitude where a lot of other issues are concerned. And you're going to see a lot of continuing changes in progress."
